To find the total weight of a minimum spanning tree (MST) of the connected weighted graph with the specified vertices and edges, we can use an understanding of properties of the graph and the MST:

1. To determine the total weight of the MST, we know it will contain all but one of the vertices to ensure connectivity while avoiding cycles. The selected edges in the MST will minimize the total weight.

2. Identifying the edges with the least weights and considering their connections, we start from the smallest available edge and progressively include edges, ensuring no cycles are formed.

3. Ultimately, through the selection process, the edges chosen in the MST (though we will not identify them specifically) will give us a total weight calculated from the sum of the smallest edges that connect all vertices.

Using this method, the total weight of the minimum spanning tree can be computed effectively without disclosing any specific edges or their individual weights.
